outcome: Signed-in and signed-out workspace presentation now share one hierarchy, and authentication separates Sign In from Create Account
owner_impact: The three primary workspace surfaces now use the same names in navigation and card titles: Control Panel, Simulation and Experiment Authoring. Each surface has one prominent primary title instead of kicker/title pairs. Signed-out Control Panel keeps the same experiment context but replaces the Save & share card with a direct Sign In action. The authentication surface defaults to Sign In with only email and password; Create Account is a separate mode that reveals first and last name only when needed.

next.text: This concrete #273 UI/UX correction is finished. The UI/UX domain returns to living/dormant status with no automatic successor; future work requires new product-use evidence.

technical_evidence: Workspace navigation and primary card titles use the exact same labels: Control Panel, Simulation and Experiment Authoring.
Control Panel has one peer-level visible title; Current experiment remains an accessible inner region without competing as the card title.
Simulation removes the Simulation/Arena kicker-title pair and uses one Simulation title.
Experiment Authoring removes the Authoring/Experiment source kicker-title pair and uses one Experiment Authoring title.
Signed-out Control Panel hides the signed-in Save & share region and exposes a direct Sign In action beside the ordinary experiment actions.
Signed-in Control Panel preserves the existing Save & share functions.
Signed-out authentication defaults to Sign In with email and password only.
Create Account is an explicit second mode; first name and last name are visible only in that mode, with a direct return to Sign In.
Signed-out account navigation is labelled Sign In; signed-in navigation remains Account.
Production responsive smoke verifies workspace hierarchy on phone, foldable, desktop and ultra-wide viewports.
Production student-onboarding smoke verifies both Sign In and Create Account presentation without creating a real account.
Scientific runtime, authoring/compiler behavior, revisions, autosave, sharing semantics, Showcase and Professor functions are unchanged.
